problems.title: The released LPIPS call omits the conversion from \([0,1]\) to \([-1,1]\)
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF p. 7; metrics_mixgs.py, lines 24–50; train_mixgs.py, lines 263–277; lpipsPyTorch/modules/networks.py, lines 40–54.
claim: Section 4.1 reports LPIPS image quality. In the current author release, metrics_mixgs.py converts RGB images to tensors in \([0,1]\), and the training evaluator clamps images to that same range. Both pass these tensors directly to the bundled LPIPS wrapper. The LPIPS authors specify inputs in \([-1,1]\), or an explicit affine conversion before feature scaling.
analysis: The bundled feature network standardizes its red channel with mean \(-0.030\) and scale \(0.458\), without any preceding range conversion. For a valid input \(x\in[0,1]\), the released and intended feature inputs are therefore \[z_{\rm release}(x)=\frac{x+0.030}{0.458},\qquad z_{\rm intended}(x)=\frac{2x-1+0.030}{0.458}.\] Their difference is \((1-x)/0.458\). A black pixel produces approximately \(0.065502\) instead of \(-2.117904\); at white, both transformations agree. This algebra establishes a preprocessing mismatch independently of the learned network weights.

The local wrapper has no hidden normalization option: it constructs LPIPS and forwards both inputs directly to its feature network. The official reference implementation separately exposes an explicit normalization option for precisely the missing \(2x-1\) operation. Identical-image distances can still vanish under either convention, so that control would not clear this defect.
result: The current released evaluators do not compute the stated LPIPS preprocessing convention. The nonlinear feature network prevents inferring either the direction of score bias or a changed ranking from the input shift alone. PSNR and SSIM do not use this LPIPS transformation. Published values require identification of the actual evaluation path and, if affected, rescoring of the relevant rendered/reference images.
assumptions: RGB image tensors enter the inspected wrapper in \([0,1]\), as produced or clamped by the identified call sites.
No claim is made that the published tables used this exact public path.
repair: Convert both images with \(2x-1\) at the two LPIPS call sites, or provide an explicit wrapper range option that applies that conversion exactly once. The rearranged red-channel expression \((x-0.485)/0.229\) verifies the intended affine map algebraically. This does not supply recomputed perceptual scores.
problems.impact_rationale: This changes the feature inputs of the released LPIPS evaluator, while actual published-score provenance and ranking effects remain unknown; the demonstrated impact is a local metric-implementation defect.
problems.existing_correction_status: An affine input-range correction is proposed; adoption in the current author release is not observed in the inspected call sites.

problems.title: The joint-stage implementation stops cross-branch derivatives through coarse attributes
problems.source_location: Eqs. (5) and (11), PDF pp. 5–6; Section 3.4, PDF p. 7; train_mixgs.py, lines 87–92 and 153–160; gaussian_renderer/__init__.py, lines 75–107.
claim: The paper jointly fine-tunes coarse Gaussians \(G_c\) and learned detail parameters \(\Phi\). Its decoded positions satisfy \(\widetilde\mu_i=\mu_i+o_i\). The current implementation detaches coarse attributes before detail encoding and detaches coarse anchors in the decoded branch, while retaining direct coarse-render gradients and stepping both parameter-group optimizers.
analysis: This changes the derivative convention. For the scalar analogue \(F(g,o)=L_c(g)+L_d(g+o)\), ordinary differentiation gives \[\partial_gF=L_c\prime(g)+L_d\prime(g+o),\] whereas detaching the decoded anchor gives only \(L_c\prime(g)\); the offset derivative remains \(L_d\prime(g+o)\). Thus merely making coarse parameters trainable does not recover decoded-branch chain-rule terms.

However, updating both groups through selected derivative paths is still a form of joint training. Neither the cited prose nor a convergence theorem requires every composite-objective derivative to be propagated. The forward anchor equation is unchanged. The observed stop-gradient choice therefore does not establish that the joint-training claim is false or that a full-gradient variant would perform better.
result: This concern is retained as a method-specification qualification, with no current paper error established. Explicitly stating the stop-gradient convention would aid reproduction; it is not evidence of failed scene reconstruction or a validated alternative optimization method.
assumptions: The assessment concerns the cited joint-training wording and the inspected derivative paths, with visibility and the other attributes held fixed in the scalar illustration.
problems.impact_rationale: Both parameter groups are updated, and no explicit full-chain-rule guarantee is contradicted; the stopped derivative is a permissible optimization convention rather than a supported error.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required by this scoped assessment; the derivative convention can be stated more explicitly.

problems.title: The advertised checkpoint resume path omits the learned MixGS representation
problems.source_location: Section 3.4, PDF p. 7; train_mixgs.py, lines 40–57 and 143–164; scene/gaussian_model.py, capture/restore; scene/mixgs_model.py, construction and save_weights/load_weights.
claim: The released training interface advertises checkpoint saving and resumption for a representation containing coarse Gaussians and a learned hash encoder/decoder. The checkpoint save statement serializes only gaussians.capture() and the iteration, while the resume branch constructs a fresh MixGSModel and restores only the Gaussian object.
analysis: GaussianModel.capture includes Gaussian tensors, Gaussian optimizer state and associated metadata; it does not contain the separately constructed encoder, decoder or their optimizer. Consequently the saved payload cannot reconstruct those learned parameters. Restoring a late iteration while retaining newly initialized detail parameters cannot continue the complete prior training state. This follows directly from serialization coverage, without executing the training program.

Separate save_weights/load_weights methods do exist, and normal scene saving writes encoder/decoder weights. This is a positive control against claiming that the representation cannot be saved at all. The checkpoint resume branch does not invoke those methods or restore the detail optimizer. A manually arranged warm start therefore differs from complete continuation through the provided interface.
result: The current checkpoint/resume path is incomplete for interrupted MixGS training. The default checkpoint list is empty, and this omission does not refute uninterrupted runs or independently saved evaluation weights. No resumed scene-quality result is claimed.
assumptions: The user requests the provided checkpoint/resume interface after the detail representation has acquired learned state.
No undocumented external restoration of the separate MixGS state is assumed.
repair: Use a complete checkpoint containing Gaussian state, encoder and decoder state dictionaries, both optimizer states, iteration, and compatible schedule/configuration metadata. Random and data-loader state is additionally needed if exact continuation is promised. This is a state-coverage proposal; uninterrupted-versus-resumed equivalence has not been tested here.
problems.impact_rationale: The omission breaks the released interrupted-run continuation contract, while default uninterrupted training and separately saved evaluation weights remain outside the affected path.
problems.existing_correction_status: Complete checkpoint-state coverage is proposed; the current save and resume branches still omit the separate learned detail state.

impact_rationale: The LPIPS input contract and checkpoint continuation contract fail in identifiable released paths, but the table-producing evaluation provenance and any changed scene-quality ranking remain unestablished. These local defects support Minor.
